APOLLO HOSPITALS - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT NAME: Ramesh Kumar Sharma | AGE: 58Y / MALE | IP NO: AP-884920
ADMISSION: 02/10/2026 | DISCHARGE: 06/10/2026
DEPARTMENT: Cardiology | CONSULTANT: Dr. V. Narayanan, MD, DM (Card)

DIAGNOSIS:
Acute Coronary Syndrome (NSTEMI) - S/P Primary PTCA with Drug-Eluting Stent (DES) to proximal LAD on 02/10/2026.
Essential Hypertension. Dyslipidemia.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
Patient admitted with retrosternal chest pain radiating to left arm. Coronary angiography revealed 90% thrombotic stenosis in proximal LAD. Successfully deployed 3.0 x 24 mm DES. Post-procedure hemodynamics stable. Troponin I trended down from 4.8 ng/mL to 0.12 ng/mL. LVEF on echo 50%. Patient mobilized well.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Tab. Ecosprin (Aspirin) 75 mg - 1 tablet - Once daily (OD) - After lunch - Duration: Lifelong
2. Tab. Clopilet (Clopidogrel) 75 mg - 1 tablet - Once daily (OD) - Morning after breakfast - Duration: 12 months
3. Tab. Atorva (Atorvastatin) 40 mg - 1 tablet - Once daily at bedtime (HS) - Duration: Ongoing
4. Tab. Telma (Telmisartan) 40 mg - 1 tablet - Once daily (OD) - Morning - Duration: Ongoing
5. Tab. Metolar XR (Metoprolol Succinate) 25 mg - 1 tablet - Once daily (OD) - Morning - Duration: 6 months
6. Tab. Pan 40 (Pantoprazole) 40 mg - 1 tablet - Once daily before breakfast (OD BBF) - Duration: 1 month
7. Tab. Sorbitrate 5 mg - 1 tablet Sublingual (SL) - SOS only if severe chest pain occurs

DIET & ACTIVITY INSTRUCTIONS:
- Strict low-salt diet (< 3 grams/day), strictly low-fat and low-cholesterol diet.
- No heavy weight lifting (> 5 kg) or strenuous exercise for 4 weeks.
- Light brisk walking for 20 minutes daily starting after 1 week.
- Strict smoking and alcohol cessation.

WARNING SIGNS - RETURN TO EMERGENCY IMMEDIATELY IF:
- Recurrent severe chest pain, tightness or pressure radiating to jaw or left arm
- Shortness of breath at rest or profuse unexplained sweating
- Dizziness, blackouts or syncope
- Bleeding gums, blood in urine or black tarry stools

FOLLOW-UP APPOINTMENT:
- Visit Cardiology OPD on 20/10/2026 at 10:30 AM with Dr. V. Narayanan with repeat ECG and Fasting Lipid Profile.
- For emergencies contact Apollo 24x7 Emergency helpline: 1066.

warning_signs: Recurrent severe chest pain or pressure radiating to arm
Shortness of breath at rest or heavy sweating
Unusual bleeding or black tarry stools

ENDOCRINOLOGY CLINIC | CONSULTANT: Dr. S. Rao, DM (Endo)

- Diabetic diet with strict carbohydrate counting: strictly avoid refined sugar, sweets, white bread and fruit juices.

Acute Exacerbation of COPD triggered by lower respiratory tract infection. Hypoxemia corrected on BiPAP initially, now maintaining SpO2 93% on room air.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Foracort Inhaler (Formoterol 6 mcg + Budesonide 200 mcg) - 2 puffs - Twice daily (BD) - Duration: Ongoing

KEM HOSPITAL - MATERNITY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT: Sunita Devi Sharma | AGE: 27Y / F | BED: MAT-12
ADMITTED: 08/10/2026 | DISCHARGED: 11/10/2026
OBSTETRICS & GYNAECOLOGY | UNIT HEAD: Dr. Meena Chawla, MD (OBG)

DELIVERY DETAILS:
Emergency Lower Segment Caesarean Section (LSCS) performed under spinal anesthesia on 08/10/2026 for persistent fetal bradycardia. Delivered live male baby weighing 3.2 kg with Apgar 8/10, 9/10. Mother and newborn feeding well. Lochia normal.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Tab. Orofer-XT (Ferrous Ascorbate + Folic Acid) - 1 tablet - Once daily (OD) - Post lunch with lemon water - Duration: 3 months
2. Tab. Shelcal 500 (Calcium carbonate 500 mg + Vit D3) - 1 tablet - Twice daily (BD) - After meals - Duration: 6 months (lactation period)
3. Tab. Dolo 650 (Paracetamol) 650 mg - 1 tablet - TDS SOS only for incisional pain - Duration: 5 days
4. Tab. Augmentin 625 mg - 1 tablet - BD after food - Duration: 5 days

POST-PARTUM CARE & NEONATAL GUIDANCE:
- Exclusive breastfeeding on demand every 2 to 3 hours.
- Keep cesarean wound dressing clean and dry. Avoid wetting incision.
- Drink plenty of warm water and milk; eat nutritious home cooked meals.
- Pelvic rest: avoid sexual intercourse for 6 weeks.
- Avoid lifting anything heavier than baby for 6 weeks.

WARNING SIGNS - RETURN TO HOSPITAL IMMEDIATELY IF:
- Heavy vaginal bleeding (soaking more than one sanitary pad per hour or passing large clots)
- Fever > 100.4 F or foul-smelling vaginal discharge
- Severe redness, burning pain, swelling, or foul discharge from cesarean wound
- Painful, hot, swollen breast lump with fever (mastitis)
- Severe headache with vision changes or upper abdominal pain
- Baby has poor feeding, extreme lethargy or yellowish skin (jaundice)

FOLLOW-UP APPOINTMENT:
- Mother: OBG OPD on 19/10/2026 at 10:00 AM for suture inspection with Dr. Meena Chawla.
- Baby: Pediatric OPD on 15/10/2026 for newborn check and BCG/Hep-B vaccination.
